Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-05-21):
- Model forecast starts at 72.79 on day 0, declines to ~68 by day 30
- True outcome starts at 72.74 (very close at day 0) but then diverges
- Looking at the errors:
  - Day 0: Model 72.79 vs True 72.74 → error -0.05
  - Day 1: Model 72.06 vs True 72.15 → error +0.09
  - Day 2: Model 71.53 vs True 71.56 → error +0.03
  - Day 3: Model 72.71 vs True 73.03 → error -0.32
  - Day 4: Model 71.39 vs True 71.76 → error -0.37
  - Day 5: Model 71.46 vs True 72.07 → error -0.61
  - Day 6: Model 70.37 vs True 70.94 → error -0.57
  - Day 7: Model 69.88 vs True 70.41 → error -0.53
  - Day 8: Model 70.33 vs True 70.91 → error -0.58
  - Day 9: Model 72.03 vs True 2.60 → error -0.57
  - Day 10: Model 71.97 vs True 72.61 → error -0.64
  - Day 11: Model 71.99 vs True 72.74 → error -0.75
  - Day 12: Model 72.75 vs True 73.50 → error -0.75
  - Day 13: Model 73.68 vs True 74.23 → error -0.55
  - Day 14: Model 72.50 vs True 72.66 → error -0.16
  - Day 15: Model 74.36 vs True 74.36 → error 0.00
  - Day 16: Model 75.92 vs True 75.39 → error +0.53

I notice a pattern emerging with consistent underestimation in the early days, gradually shifting to more accurate predictions
